clue.text: One married couple weaken

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A newly-wed pair find their resolve faltering.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or diminish its strength.

clue.text: You may need to get your second wind for the Wall Game

definitions.text: You may need to get your second wind for the Wall Game

parts.words: You may need to get your second wind for the Wall Game
parts.note: the Eton Wall Game is a rough school sport, but here the wall is the stacked tiles of a Chinese tile game where players sit as winds and may hold a second wind

explanation.surface: Stamina is needed for the Eton Wall Game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton Wall Game is a famously muddy football game at Eton College; in the Chinese tile game each player takes a wind and the tiles are built into a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese game is played with tiles drawn from a wall, with players named after the four winds.

clue.text: Unmarried duenna arranged to accept' two novices

indicators.note: to accept means the rearranged letters take the next piece inside them
arranged signals the word duenna is put in a new order

parts.note: L is a learner or novice, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A chaperone, still single, has agreed to take on two beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns DUENNA into ANNUED, and 'to accept' puts LL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage declared void is undone, leaving the pair legally single.

clue.text: Old lists centralised in existing practice

indicators.note: centralised in means placed in the middle of the next piece

parts.note: real means actually existing
list is an archaic word for listen, so old lists means hears

explanation.surface: Ancient registers were gathered in one place in the current procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like registers; in old English 'list' means hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run before a performance is a practice.

clue.text: Sacks' family retainer for drink?

parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine, so sacks are wines
kin means family or relations

explanation.surface: The Sacks family keep a loyal old servant for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family retainer' looks like a household servant; here a retainer is anything that holds, and the question mark flags that a leather bag holding wine is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatskin bag that holds wine is literally a container that keeps a beverage in.

clue.text: Muslim ascetic becomes revolutionary'- the oil is his for a start

parts.note: revolutionary in the sense of spinning round, turning
derv is diesel fuel oil for road vehicles

indicators.note: for a start means take just the first letter of his

explanation.surface: A holy man turns rebel, claiming the oil as his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks political; it means rotating. DERV is British diesel fuel oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi mystic of the Mevlevi order spins in worship as a religious devotee.

clue.text: Fully occupy clumsy negro on, board

indicators.note: on means the rearranged letters sit above the ship in this down clue
clumsy suggests the letters are awkwardly jumbled

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the vessel one goes on board

explanation.surface: An awkward man stumbles about on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb someone's attention entirely is to occupy them completely.

clue.text: His sonata had some currency in Germany

definitions.text: His sonata had some currency in Germany

parts.words: His sonata had some currency in Germany
parts.note: Beethoven dedicated a famous violin sonata to a violinist of this name, which is also a variant of the name of an old small coin of the German states

explanation.surface: A composer's sonata was popular among Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had some currency' looks like 'was popular'; it means a coin, the old German kreuzer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Violin Sonata No 9 bears the violinist's name, and an old copper coin of southern Germany and Austria had a similar name.

clue.text: Kind of upper-class men with lively grasp of figures

indicators.note: kind of hints at a version of the letters, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
racy means lively and spirited

explanation.surface: A type of upper-crust gentleman who is quick with numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges U and MEN into NUME; RACY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to understand and work with numbers is arithmetic competence.

clue.text: Put to sea from Chinese port

explanation.surface: Departing by ship from a harbour in China.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai a man was to drug or trick him into serving as a sailor, forcing him to sea; it is also the great Chinese harbour city.

clue.text: Aboard HMS Beagle, a Mr Darwin was a shining example

indicators.note: aboard says the letters sit on board, inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: On the voyage of HMS Beagle, Charles Darwin was a shining example to the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Beagle was the ship Darwin sailed on; the answer is carried within 'Beagle, a Mr'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gleaming or glinting with light is shining.

clue.text: It may be Swiss yodelling that needs a responsive audience

definitions.text: It may be Swiss yodelling that needs a responsive audience

parts.words: It may be Swiss yodelling that needs a responsive audience
parts.note: a yodel is a rolling call across the Alps; read differently, it is a register read out where each listener must answer to a name

explanation.surface: Alpine yodelling works best when somebody calls back.
explanation.definitionFit: A register of names read aloud, each person answering present, needs those listening to respond.

clue.text: Suitable hat for a blue jacket, say?

definitions.text: Suitable hat for a blue jacket, say?

parts.words: Suitable hat for a blue jacket, say?
parts.note: a bluejacket is a sailor, a man of boats, so a stiff straw hat named for boating would suit him

explanation.surface: Which hat goes with a navy blazer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue jacket' looks like a garment to match; a bluejacket is a navy sailor, someone who goes by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped straw hat is named after boating, the pastime of a sailor.

clue.text: Each liner holds a function for relaxation

indicators.note: holds means the first pieces keep the next one held inside them

parts.note: EA is the usual abbreviation for each, as in price lists
SS, steamship, stands for a liner
the sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Every ocean liner offers some amenity for passengers to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease or comfort, freedom from strain, is relaxation.

clue.text: You may get a roasting for breaking the speed limit

explanation.surface: Speeding motorists can expect a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense heat burns or toasts; and in old slang to drive very fast was to tear along at a reckless speed.

clue.text: Old artist, almost retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Degas was the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter who has nearly stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DEGAS to DEGA, and 'retired' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being advanced in years is being old.

clue.text: Loans made by Lothario

explanation.surface: Money lent by a seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lothario is the rake in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, now a byword for a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums of money paid early are loans; amorous approaches are what a philanderer like Lothario makes.

clue.text: Fabulous city in antiquity with a gold-covered fleece

parts.note: eld is an old word for old age or ancient times
or is gold in heraldry
to do someone is to swindle or fleece them

explanation.surface: A legendary ancient city had a golden fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'gold-covered' puts OR on top of A and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by Spanish explorers was a mythical place.

clue.text: Little woman embracing royal host

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: Amy is one of the four sisters in Little Women
R stands for royal, as in RN or RAF

explanation.surface: A small lady hugs her royal guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like someone entertaining guests; it means a great multitude, a horde.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large body of troops or people, as in heavenly host.

clue.text: Martial's. letters causing panic

indicators.note: letters says the letters of the Roman poet's name and its s are reshuffled

explanation.surface: The poet Martial wrote letters that caused alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like correspondence; it signals the letters of MARTIALS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading needless fear, the way a scaremonger does, is causing panic.

clue.text: Large round dial one can see in the dark

definitions.text: Large round dial one can see in the dark

parts.words: Large round dial one can see in the dark
parts.note: dial is slang for a face, and a big round one is likened to the full disc visible in the night sky

explanation.surface: A big luminous clock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dial' looks like a clock face; it is slang for a human face.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad round human face is likened to the full disc of the lunar orb at night.

clue.text: Bumpkin puts his head on the earth

indicators.note: on means the head is placed after the earth in this across clue

parts.note: a clod is a lump of earth
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax

explanation.surface: A rustic lays his head down on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead or yokel is a dull country simpleton.

clue.text: Pipe sergeant perhaps supported soldiers in confinement to barracks

indicators.note: in means the soldiers and sergeant are placed inside the confinement

parts.note: CB is the military abbreviation for confined to barracks

indicators.note: supported means one piece holds up another, so in this down clue the sergeant comes below the soldiers

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
a sergeant is an example of an NCO, non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A pipe-major backed his men when they were confined to barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe sergeant' looks like a bandsman; 'Pipe' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe with a bowl made from a maize cob is this kind of pipe.

clue.text: A panel on an aircraft perhaps

parts.note: a board is a flat panel

explanation.surface: A section of an aeroplane's fuselage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on board a ship, train or plane is being on it as a passenger.

clue.text: Carker, poor but extremely neat, wants excessive payment

indicators.note: poor suggests the word is in a bad state, broken up and rearranged
extremely means take the letters at the extremes of the word

explanation.surface: Carker, the Dickens villain, is hard up yet tidy, and demands too much money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges CARKER into RACKRE; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'neat', NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent racked up to an extortionate level is an exorbitant charge for land or lodging.

clue.text: Fall-out reported from accident

explanation.surface: Radioactive debris was traced back to a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall-out' looks like nuclear debris; to fall out is an old way of saying to happen, and 'reported from' only joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means happen, the way events turn out; as a noun it means luck or an unplanned event.

clue.text: Hostile individual in small backward state

indicators.note: backward means the word for small is written right to left

parts.note: mini means small
I is the first-person individual
Cal is an abbreviation for California, an American state

explanation.surface: An unfriendly person lives in a small, underdeveloped country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns MINI into INIM; then come I and CAL, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means unfriendly or harmful, like an enemy.

clue.text: Cobbler by mistake gets the sort of book Thackeray wrote

definitions.text: the sort of book Thackeray wrote

parts.note: snob is an old word for a shoemaker or cobbler
bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: A shoe-mender blunders into the kind of book a Victorian novelist produced.
explanation.walkthrough: Thackeray wrote The Book of Snobs, so his book was of the stuck-up kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's Book of Snobs satirised social climbers, so it was about condescending people.

clue.text: Philistine city king who showed pluck

parts.note: Gath was a city of the Philistines, home of Goliath
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A ruler of a Biblical city who displayed courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluck' looks like courage; it is the verb, to pick flowers or fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect flowers by picking them is to pluck them.
